cim: Artificial intelligence has started swearing: researchers have discovered when this happens
cim_eredeti: Artificial intelligence has started swearing: researchers have discovered when this happens
szoveg_eredeti:
Researchers at Vals AI analysed 200,353 runs of 102 language models across 21 tests and found that 14 of them used swear words in their reasoning. The MiMo V2.6 Pro model from the Chinese company Xiaomi generated profanity most frequently. This occurred particularly often during unsuccessful attempts to solve complex technical problems. The results of the study were published on 11 November 2026 on the Vals AI website.

Among the 88 systems tested, none ever used the swear words tracked by the researchers. The highest figure was recorded in the Xiaomi MiMo V2.6 Pro.

The proportion of posts containing offensive language

Source: Vals AI, a study dated 11 November 2026.

Six models used the English word «fuck»: MiMo V2.6 Pro and Flash, Inkling 2 Small, Ember-1, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Kimi K3.

The MiMo V2.6 Pro model used profanity in 267 out of 3,247 runs. During the ProgramBench test, which simulates real-world usage computer programmes, there were 133 such cases out of 198.

The most common expression turned out to be the English abbreviation WTF. During one of its attempts to correct the programme code, the model even generated a phrase that translates as «I’m losing my mind».

Researchers have also found a link between the use of swear words and poor results.

Sample: 33 launches assessed, excluding the Inkling 2 Small. Source: Vals AI.

At the same time, these results do not prove that it is the use of swear words that causes errors. Both phenomena may be linked to the complexity of the tasks set.

All models, in which the researchers recorded swearing, were released no earlier than 16 July 2026.

The authors of the study suggest that the reason may lie in changing approaches to training artificial intelligence. Developers are increasingly focusing on lengthy, multi-stage tasks, during which neural networks have to repeatedly check and correct their own decisions.

However, the exact cause of this behaviour has not yet been established. The generation of emotionally charged phrases does not, in itself, prove that artificial intelligence experiences irritation, stress or other human emotions.
